property_summary: If transfer(...) returns (does not revert) then it must return true and leave c.from and c.caddress unchanged.

If transfer(tos, vals) does not revert for non-empty tos then it returns (i.e. does not revert) only when msg.sender equals c.from and the input arrays have equal positive length; when it succeeds the stored addresses c.from and c.caddress remain unchanged.
If transfer is invoked with a non-empty tos array and matching vals length by any caller, then either it reverts or it returns true (i.e., successful non-reverting call implies true).

If transfer(...) is called with tos.length > 0 and vals.length == tos.length and msg.sender equals the stored c.from (which is a public address), then the call either reverts or returns true (i.e., non-reverting implies true).
When run by the contract that equals c.from and given non-empty arrays of equal length, c.transfer either reverts or returns true (i.e., non-reverting implies true).

If transfer returns normally then it returns true and does not change c.from or c.caddress (their getters remain equal to their pre-call values); if it reverts then from/caddress also remain unchanged.
If transfer returns (does not revert) then it must return true.
If transfer returns normally then it must not modify c.from or c.caddress (their getters remain equal to their pre-call values).

For any non-empty equal-length inputs where all v[i] are such that multiplication by 1e18 doesn't overflow, calling transfer either reverts or returns true; if it returns true then c.from and c.caddress remain equal to their pre-call values.
For any non-empty equal-length inputs that satisfy the contract's internal multiplication check, transfer either reverts or returns true and leaves c.from unchanged.
